items.title: Vinesh Phogat case: Delhi HC says WFI must balance interests of nation and women athletes returning after childbirth
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Thursday remarked that the Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) must come up with guidelines to enable participation of female athletes returning after maternity leave. Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma said that a balance must be struck between the interests of the country and the athlete. The Court made the remark while hearing Olympian Vinesh Phogat’s plea seeking directions to allow her to participate in the trials for the Senior World Wrestling Championship scheduled on September 14. Senior Advocate Rajshekhar Rao appeared for Phogat and told the Bench that the WFI has displayed “absolute arbitrariness” in the case and she was informed of the selection criteria only on September 7. “Effectively, it means I am out of reckoning for two more years and I am finished as an athlete,” he said. The counsel appearing for the WFI told the Bench that Phogat has not been banned from participation. He said that the medal winners from 2025 and 2026 are eligible for selection for this year’s World Championship and Phogat can participate at the state and national levels and make her way up. items.summary: The Bombay High Court on Wednesday sought the assistance of the Maharashtra Advocate General in a plea challenging the recent amendments to the Maharashtra Caste Certificate Act, 2000. [Halbi Adim Jamat Mandal, Yavatmal v. State of Maharashtra & Ors.] The case was listed before a division bench of Justices Anil Kilor and Rajnish Vyas at Nagpur. Justice Anil Kilor and Justice Rajnish Vyas The latest amendments to the Act introduce statutory definitions for "fake" and "false" caste and validity certificates. items.title: CJI Surya Kant to attend NLSIU convocation on October 17
items.summary: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant will attend the 34th convocation of National Law School of India University (NLSIU) on October 17. The University's Executive Council and General Council approved the new date on Wednesday following weeks of uncertainty over whether the ceremony, originally scheduled for September 12, would be held at all. The convocation was cancelled in August after graduating students rejected a demand to issue a public statement inviting the CJI to the ceremony. It later emerged that the demand came days after students had already agreed to a convocation with the CJI present. More than 700 current and former NLSIU students had objected to the CJI and Bar Council of India (BCI) Chairman Manan Kumar Mishra attending the ceremony. The objection followed the BCI's August 13 decisions to halt and, within hours, restore enrolment for NALSAR Hyderabad's graduating batch over its own objection to CJI Kant's presence at its convocation. NLSIU later cancelled the convocation before deciding that it will hold the same with the CJI being present. Students have the option to obtain their degrees at the convocation or in-absentia.

items.title: Supreme Court asks Centre to respond to plea seeking safeguards for minors on social media
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday issued notice to the Central government on a public interest litigation (PIL) petition seeking safeguards, including firewalls, to protect children below eighteen years from exploitation on social media and other digital platforms. A bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was hearing the plea filed by NGO Just Rights for Children Alliance (JRCA). As per the petition, the absence of an effective mechanism to verify the age and authority of users exposes children to online grooming, sexual exploitation, digital trafficking, sextortion, cyberbullying and exposure to age-inappropriate content. Justice Joymalya Bagchi, CJI Surya Kant and Justice V Mohana While issuing notice, Justice Bagchi orally observed that there should be safeguards like firewalls to protect children in the digital environment. The plea was filed raising concerns over minors being allowed to independently create and maintain social media accounts despite their incapacity to enter into contracts under Section 11 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872. items.title: Judiciary not averse to criticism but it must come through appropriate forum: Supreme Court in NCERT textbook case
items.summary: The Supreme Court recently observed that the judiciary is not averse to criticism, but made it clear that such criticism must be voiced through an appropriate forum and not find its way into school curriculum without verification. A Bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana made the observation while disposing of its suo motu case concerning a chapter titled The Role of the Judiciary in our Society in the NCERT Grade 8 Social Science textbook called Exploring Society: India and Beyond. CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, Justice V Mohana "The Judiciary, as an institution, is not, and cannot be, averse to criticism. Fair, informed and constructive critique of judicial functioning is a legitimate and necessary feature of a vibrant constitutional democracy, contributing to institutional accountability and self-correction. What is required, however, is that such criticism be voiced through the appropriate forum and in a fair, rational mechanism, and not find its way, without verification, into a school curriculum meant for impressionable minds," the Court said in its order. The Court ruled that IIT Bombay could not have pursued the patent application on its own after it executed a worldwide assignment deed in July 2017 to transfer to Patil the full and exclusive right, title and interest in the invention. The Court rejected the argument that the deed of assignment did not extend to India but only to the United States. It, thus, ordered the Controller to process the patent application, with Patil as the applicant. items.title: Sharia body can't decide whether Muslim woman is divorced: Chhattisgarh High Court
items.summary: A private Sharia body has no legal authority to decide whether a Muslim woman is legally divorced or to determine her marital status, the Chhattisgarh High Court recently held. In a judgment delivered on September 7, Justice Amitendra Kishore Prasad said that such adjudicatory power must flow from a law enacted by a competent legislature and cannot be assumed by a private religious institution. The Court was dealing with a challenge to a January 2022 communication issued by the Idara-E-Shariya Islami Court at Raipur which declared that the petitioner, a Muslim woman, had been divorced by her husband. " Religion may guide an individual's conscience and personal faith, but no religious institution or private body can be permitted to assume the authority of a Court established by law or to use religious belief as a means of determining or enforcing the legal status and rights of an individual. The rule of law and the constitutional framework remain paramount, " the Court said.
